gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Minn Kota's PCL applies no temperature compensation in lithium mode, while a typical LiFePO4 trolling battery's own BMS refuses charge below 32°F (Redodo: resumes only above 41°F). So in cold weather the battery, not the charger, decides whether an onboard charger left plugged in overnight puts any charge back.
standout_why: I compared five pages. Minn Kota PCL Features/Specs (cited) covers per-bank chemistry, lithium wake-up and the 14.5 V maximum, but says nothing about lithium in the cold. Minn Kota Battery Charger Selection Guide (cited) covers series batteries, one bank per battery and 12 V systems only, and gives no low-temperature guidance. BoatDealsDirect has standby wake-up and Victron's 14.2 V figure, but nothing on charging below 32°F. Williams Wordsmith never mentions cold-weather charging or a low-temperature cutoff. I could not open NOCO's cited specs page (no.co returned HTTP 403) or GearRanking (TLS error). The rivals already cover wake-up, the 14.5 V maximum and the lack of support for single 24 V/36 V lithium batteries. None ties the charger to the battery's charge cutoff at freezing.
decides: For any of the multi-bank chargers ChatGPT named, the fact confirms the 'one bank per 12 V battery, chemistry set per bank' plan. It adds one condition that decides whether charging works at all: an angler charging lithium in late fall, winter or early spring needs a battery whose BMS has a low-temperature charge cutoff, or self-heating. No charger setting replaces that. The PCL's temperature compensation does not apply to lithium, and Minn Kota publishes no cold limit. A practical pairing is a PCL or GENPRO bank on a Redodo low-temp-cutoff battery, or the Redodo self-heating model for below-freezing launches. Expect no charge until the battery warms above 41°F. The PCL's 14.5 V maximum sits 0.1 V under Redodo's recommended 14.6 V charger. Minn Kota itself tells buyers to check that against the battery maker's spec.

findings.label: Temperature compensation in lithium mode
findings.value: Not applied: 'not required for Lithium Batteries'
findings.source_title: Using the Precision Charger Lithium (PCL) (2021-present) – Minn Kota
findings.note: The page also says that in lithium mode 'the charger will stay in Bulk Mode until the process is complete'. The only temperature figure it gives is a 122°F maximum recommended charging room temperature. It states no low-temperature limit for lithium. This page was in ChatGPT's results but was not cited.

findings.label: Lithium standby wake-up
findings.value: Auto Start restarts a lithium battery from standby 'a set number of times' (count not published)
findings.note: Minn Kota: 'If the BMS detects an undesirable condition it will electrically disconnect the battery terminal from the lithium cells… This is called Standby Mode.' The charger may show 'check connection'. 'Most lithium batteries require that you remove all electrical connections to the battery before it will turn back on.'

findings.label: Maximum charge voltage
findings.note: Minn Kota asks buyers to 'ensure our Max voltage of 14.5V meets the specifications of the Battery Manufacturer'. The same page says 'not compatible with single 24V and 36V Lithium Batteries.' The cited PCL specs page also gives 14.5 V maximum.

findings.label: Battery type per bank, and series wiring
findings.value: Each bank set separately (Lithium, Flooded, AGM/High Performance AGM, Equalize). The setting is kept in memory when AC/DC power is removed. Series or parallel banks charge without removing jumpers.
findings.source_title: Using the Precision Charger Lithium (PCL) (2021-present) – Minn Kota
findings.note: Quote: 'each charger bank must be set to match the connected battery type'. The charger 'can charge independent batteries or combinations of batteries hooked in series or parallel' without disconnecting switches or jump wires.

findings.label: Series batteries and banks
findings.value: Batteries wired in series cannot be charged with one bank. Minn Kota chargers are for 12 V battery systems only.
findings.source_title: Battery Charger Selection Guide – Minn Kota
findings.note: This cited rival already has it. Included as the baseline for how banks map to batteries. The guide also says 'Lithium batteries can shut themselves off after extensive use or under certain conditions.'
